title: How to talk to statues — Joe Reeve, ElevenLabs
talk_summary: A growth-org talk about a viral 'talk to statues' demo built by stitching existing APIs together in a two-hour vibe-coding session, followed by an audience discussion on voice-interface UX (interruption, skim-listening, parallel visual+voice output). It contains almost no engineering practice for agent orchestration, review, or cost control.

takeaways.technique: Intermediary agent between user and worker agent
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of talking directly to a coding agent, route the request through a lightweight 'product manager' agent that then triggers the coding agent, so the conversational layer and the doing layer are separated.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I want to talk to like a product manager agent that then goes off and triggers my coding agent to go and do things

takeaways.technique: Truncate agent output at interruption point using audio timestamps
takeaways.what_they_do: When a user interrupts mid-response, use the known playback timestamp to cut the generated transcript at that point and discard the rest, rather than appending the new user message after the full stale response.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we do have the timestamps... we could actually just go and edit the transcript that's coming back and say, well, no, they interrupted at this point

takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than tool-calling inline, run a separate loop that repeatedly re-reads the conversation transcript asking 'do you have anything to add?', so a second agent can surface suggestions asynchronously.
